$description: SOLAR Spinner: public API, platform states, slots and style recipe in token names. Generated by @bwp-web/codegen from docs/solar-web. Do not edit; decisions go in spec/overlay/, and the ones applied are listed under overlay.

gap.reason: Same value, governed token: a gap Figma leaves unbound at 0 is the none of its family, and SOLAR picks the family by direction, as its own bound gaps do: a horizontal auto layout's gap is an inset, a vertical one's a stack (the Foundations agent reference and the Spatial chapter). Decided once here, as the paddings are.

paddingTop.reason: Same value, governed token: a padding Figma leaves unbound at 0 is inset.none, SOLAR's token for no inset. It is the one answer in every component, so it is decided once here and raised with SOLAR once, as a whole, not per component.

borderColor.reason: Figma binds the default indicator's colour to Spatial:border/strong, the stroke *width* variable, which holds no colour; the recipe reports it as misbound. color.border.strong is the colour of the same name, and the inverse style's indicator uses its inverse (color.border.inverse.strong), as its track pairs border.subtle with border.inverse.subtle. Raised with SOLAR to rebind.

docs.description: Circular indeterminate loading indicator. 6 variants: size (sm, md, lg) × style (default, inverse) — inverse is for dark and inverse surfaces. Non-interactive. Pair with visually-hidden text or aria-busy on the region it covers; for known progress use Progress Bar, for layout placeholders use Skeleton.
figmaIssues: Non-color variable bound as a color: `border.strong`.

rules.reason: Each platform's own indeterminate spinner, restyled by the recipe: size, stroke width, track and indicator colours. Its motion stays the platform's, because Figma draws a still frame and SOLAR has no token for a spinner's rotation. MUI draws the track with enableTrackSlot.
`style` is React's inline-style prop, so a component cannot take it as a SOLAR prop. `variant` is what Button calls its appearance axis too.

Figma binds the default indicator's colour to Spatial:border/strong, the stroke *width* variable, which holds no colour; the recipe reports it as misbound. color.border.strong is the colour of the same name, and the inverse style's indicator uses its inverse (color.border.inverse.strong), as its track pairs border.subtle with border.inverse.subtle. Raised with SOLAR to rebind.
